2-2.title: Asymmetric fades and recoveries
2-2.hypothesis:
Fading and recovery may have unequal predictable persistence. Separate positive/negative slopes and trailing displacement test this.

Development feedback available before this hypothesis: [{"attempt": "attempt-001", "group_MAE": 1.2577260893238156, "worst_group": 1.7260980576240144}, {"attempt": "attempt-002", "group_MAE": 1.2286967795825008, "worst_group": 1.6533308691555735}, {"attempt": "attempt-003", "group_MAE": 1.2157744053119888, "worst_group": 1.6225962561123695}]

This attempt tests a distinct explanation/ablation. All reserved groups remain unscored. A failure to beat the incumbent rejects predictive benefit rather than proving absence of the underlying physical process.

Decision rationale: Noise-gated trend improves persistence but remains slightly worse than flexible control. Test whether fades and recoveries need different responses.
2-2.equation: offset(input) + scale(input) * sum_j coef[j] * named_basis[j](input); all named bases defined in run.py; optional correction clipping/nonnegative output explicitly in state.
